findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the cache lifecycle: specify whether attempt 1 WRITES credited-criterion verdicts to the cache (needed to seed the control arm) while only bypassing cache READS to force exhaustion, and enumerate exactly when the cache is written vs read across attempt-1 and both resume arms.
evidence: Step 1: 'disable/bypass the verdict cache in-harness so exhaustion is reproducible'
Step 5: 'CONTROL — plain re-run (locust behavior: cache-seeded only; re-enable cache for both arms)'
findings.finding: The cache lifecycle is contradictory across sections: step 1 says 'disable/bypass the verdict cache in-harness' for the forced-exhaustion run, but step 5 arm A is 'CONTROL — plain re-run (locust behavior: cache-seeded only; re-enable cache for both arms)'. If attempt 1 ran with the cache disabled, the resume arms have no attempt-1-written cache to be 'seeded' from, so the control arm cannot reproduce locust cache-seeded behavior.
scenarios: Executor disables cache in attempt 1, then re-enables for resume, finds the cache empty, and the 'cache-seeded' control arm behaves identically to a cold run — invalidating the A/B contrast
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify: 'Attempt 1 bypasses cache READS (to force full re-search / exhaustion) but WRITES verdicts for banked PASSes; both resume arms then READ that seeded cache — Control = cache-only, Treatment = cache + exclusion summary.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the overlap-match rule: state whether a 'repeat' is an exact-argument match vs normalized (canonical path, trimmed grep pattern) match, and how reads/greps/dir-lists are each counted.
evidence: 're-search overlap rate (tool calls in attempt 2 repeating attempt-1 arguments)'
A derived metric with no computation/aggregation protocol is an E2 data-design ambiguity
findings.finding: The headline metric 're-search overlap rate' has no stated computation protocol — 'tool calls in attempt 2 repeating attempt-1 arguments' does not define what counts as a repeat (exact argument string match? normalized/canonicalized file paths? equivalent-but-differently-spelled grep patterns? directory-listing overlap?).
scenarios: Executor counts a re-read of the same file under a normalized path as non-overlapping, inflating/deflating the treatment effect
Two runs of the review disagree on the overlap number because 'repeating' was interpreted differently
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'A tool call counts as an overlap when its (tool, canonicalized-path OR exact-pattern) tuple appeared in attempt 1; overlap rate = overlapping attempt-2 calls / total attempt-2 calls, computed per criterion and aggregated.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the decision rule for 'measurably beat' (e.g. treatment overlap rate lower on BOTH tickets by >=X percentage points, or frame it explicitly as a descriptive/directional PoC with no statistical claim given N=2).
evidence: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
'measurably reduce re-search overlap and steps-to-verdict'
subjective term 'measurably' with no threshold (F1 check a)
findings.finding: The verdict acceptance criterion asks whether the exclusion list 'measurably beat[s]' plain resume, but neither 'measurably' nor any decision threshold is defined; with only >=2 tickets there is no stated rule for what delta constitutes a positive result.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?' and Why: 'measurably reduce re-search overlap'
scenarios: Attempt 2B shows a 5% overlap reduction on one ticket and 0% on the other; author and reviewer disagree whether that is a 'measurable' win
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'This is a directional PoC (N=2); report per-ticket deltas and call it a win only if treatment reduces overlap AND steps-to-verdict on both tickets — no statistical significance is claimed.'

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no s' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reuse/extend docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py (which already does pai_tools tool-wrapping transcript capture + step-floor-forced exhaustion) as the harness base rather than building capture/exhaustion from scratch, or state explicitly why a fresh harness is needed.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam) to log every tool call with full arguments (file paths read, grep patterns, dirs listed)'

docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py:49-90 — _wrap() logs {tool, args, kwargs, result_len, is_error, is_empty_sentinel, result_preview}; _patch_factory patches pai_tools filesystem_tools/grounding_tools/rebar_tools
docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py:101-107 — 'Force a cheap, bounded run: lower the verifier step floor' via _completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS = floor
diag_runaway_transcript.py docstring lines 3-8 states the same blocker the plan restates: 'the durable gate-error record... deliberately HASHES tool arguments and drops results'
FP7 inapplicable: both the existing script and this plan are throwaway experiments (not production), so the 'rebuild-a-reference-for-production is intended' carve-out does not apply
findings.finding: The harness plans to build transcript-capture (step 2) and forced-exhaustion (step 3) from scratch, but docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py already implements both: it monkeypatches the real verifier tool factories (pai_tools.filesystem_tools/grounding_tools/rebar_tools) with a logger that records tool name, full args/kwargs, result preview, is_error and is_empty to a local JSONL, and it lowers the step floor (_completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS via REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS) to force a cheap exhaustion. The plan does not reference or reuse it.
scenarios: Author re-derives the pai_tools monkeypatch wrapper and step-floor override already working in diag_runaway_transcript.py, spending PoC time rebuilding solved plumbing
Subtle divergence (e.g. different arg-truncation or sentinel classification) makes the new harness's overlap metrics non-comparable to the existing diagnostic's transcripts
findings.suggested_fix: In the Protocol, cite docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py as the starting point: its _wrap/_patch_factory transcript logger and _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS override already cover steps 2-3; the new work is the cache toggle, the per-criterion frontier extractor, the exclusion-summary prompt injection, and the A/B resume driver.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a validity gate: after forcing exhaustion, assert the attempt-1 FAIL is insufficiency-only (all unmet carry the framework evidence_sufficient:false marker) and discard/re-select the ticket if a refutation appears, so both resume arms measure the intended regime.
evidence: Step 3: 'FAILs insufficiency-only with a partial bank'
Parent design (locust) only auto-resumes when _insufficiency_only(result) is True (every unmet criterion carries evidence_sufficient:false)
The plan states the outcome as a goal but adds no check that the forced FAIL actually classified as insufficiency-only
findings.finding: The protocol assumes the reduced-budget attempt-1 FAILs 'insufficiency-only' (the condition that makes it a valid model of the parent auto-resume path), but nothing guards that the induced FAIL is insufficiency-only rather than carrying a genuine refutation; a refutation FAIL would make the whole resume comparison invalid.
scenarios: Reduced budget causes the verifier to mint an unmet criterion that reconcile treats as a refutation; attempt-2's comparison then measures resume behavior the parent design would never trigger

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a repetition/variance-control plan (e.g. multiple paired runs per ticket, or fixed-seed/temperature=0 where the runner allows) so the A-vs-B overlap and PASS-per-step deltas are attributable to the exclusion list rather than verifier run-to-run variance, and state how the verdict handles overlapping ranges.
evidence: Step 6 metrics are 'A vs B' with no repetition count
AC: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
The verifier is an LLM agent whose search path is nondeterministic run-to-run
findings.finding: The experiment draws a 'measurably beats' conclusion from a single control-vs-treatment run pair per ticket over only 2 tickets, against a stochastic LLM verifier whose per-run tool-call choices vary — so observed overlap-rate / PASS-per-step deltas cannot be distinguished from run-to-run variance, weakening the fitness of the verdict for the named question.
findings.location: Protocol steps 5-6 and Acceptance criteria (verdict comment)
scenarios: Treatment shows lower overlap purely because that run happened to search differently, not because of the exclusion list
n=2 tickets both happen to favor one arm by chance
